title: North Korea: What's the Deal?
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant examine North Korea: the latest inter-Korean summit at the DMZ and talk of denuclearization, the Korean War armistice, the Kim dynasty from Kim Il Sung through Kim Jong Il to Kim Jong Un, the Soviet and Chinese roles, the juche philosophy, daily life and repression, the Dennis Rodman visits, and the options (prevention, turning the screws, decapitation, acceptance) for dealing with the North's nuclear program. The episode closes with a listener mail correction about walrus water temperatures.

segments.title: Opening banter and latest North Korea news
segments.summary: Hosts joke about the episode's timing and Kim Jong Un's unusual hair rules, then discuss the recent inter-Korean summit at the DMZ, talk of denuclearization and ending the Korean War, skepticism about North Korea's intentions, the dismantled loudspeakers, and the THAAD missile defense test.

segments.title: Latest developments and skepticism
segments.summary: Discussion of why the North's reversal is surprising, including a reported nuclear test site destruction, whether the sanctions worked, and whether Kim Jong Un's shift is genuine or a ruse.

segments.title: Kim Jong Nam assassination and break
segments.summary: The hosts describe Kim Jong Un's half brother Kim Jong Nam, who was killed in 2017 after being attacked with a nerve agent at an airport, and speculate about the motive.

segments.title: Division of Korea and Kim Il Sung's rise
segments.summary: Japanese annexation of Korea ends with World War II, and the peninsula is split at the 38th parallel between US and Soviet influence. Kim Il Sung is installed by the Soviets, and the hosts question whether his resistance credentials were genuine.

segments.title: Korean War and MacArthur
segments.summary: North Korea invades the South in 1950 with Soviet approval, the US and South Korea push back, MacArthur pushes north, Truman fires him after clashes over pursuing China, and China enters the war after the Soviets decline to help.

segments.title: Juche ideology and Kim Il Sung's purges
segments.summary: The Korean War leads Kim Il Sung to purge rivals and build a personality cult. The juche philosophy of self-reliance is explained, and the hosts describe North Korea as a hereditary dictatorship rather than a genuine communist state.

segments.title: Kim Jong Il era and Dennis Rodman
segments.summary: Kim Jong Il succeeds his father, having kidnapped a South Korean director and actress for propaganda films. Economic collapse after the Soviet Union falls brings famine. Kim Jong Un takes over, and Dennis Rodman's visits are discussed.

segments.title: Life inside North Korea
segments.summary: Description of the isolation: state-set radios, jammed broadcasts, labor camps with three-generation punishment, mandated hairstyles, a military of about 1.2 million active personnel, short life expectancy and height compared with South Korea, blackouts, and mandatory learning sessions.

segments.title: Pop culture and smuggled media
segments.summary: Smuggled South Korean soap operas, USB-modified DVD players, and cannabis being legal in North Korea. The hosts digress into Bob Marley.

segments.title: Policy options: prevention, turning the screws, decapitation, acceptance
segments.summary: The hosts review four approaches to North Korea. A preemptive attack is rejected due to mass casualties in Seoul and Tokyo and North Korea's chemical and nuclear arsenal. Decapitation and turning the screws are weighed, and acceptance with a denuclearization framework is discussed alongside Moon Jae-in's South Korea and the US presence.

segments.title: Walrus correction listener mail
segments.summary: Listener Erica Schreiber corrects the hosts: walruses can survive in air at negative temperatures, not in water. The hosts close with plugs for the site and social media.
